entities.name: PMID:25070754
observations: 2015 pediatric ICU observational pre/post study examined COMFORT-B responsiveness after pharmacological interventions; 747 paired observations from 180 patients.
Mean score decreased from 20.0 (SD 3.7) before intervention to 14.1 (SD 4.7) after; multilevel analysis estimated a 6-point decline (p<0.0001).

After intervention, 74% of scores were below 17, the study's threshold indicating adequate comfort; no formal independent patient-centered anchor or minimum clinically important difference was reported in the abstract.

entities.name: COMFORT-B treatment response
observations: In pediatric intensive care routine-care data (180 patients; 747 paired assessments), COMFORT-B fell by an estimated 6 points after analgesic/sedative pharmacological intervention (p<0.0001); 74% fell below 17 afterward.
Evidence demonstrates treatment-associated responsiveness, but not definitive causal attribution or an independently anchored minimum clinically important difference.
